question_summary: Does the AoE direction show a LOCAL Class K signature in its dark-sector ring-down trajectory, distinct from cosmic average?

description: Direction-dependent Class K signature on synthetic substrate
interpretation: This shifts the framework reading: the AoE direction's local Class K signature is the consequence of OUR OBSERVATION FRAME being off-centre on the substrate ring (with eccentricity ~ eps_AoE), NOT a literal directional perturbation of substrate density. The substrate is isotropic at the cascade level; the frame is off-centre.
load_bearing_consequence: AoE direction is the radial-offset direction OF OUR OBSERVER FRAME relative to substrate centre. AoE is the pin-slot offset direction. The 18.3 deg AoE-dipole separation is the bundle-aperture of OUR observation point relative to substrate isotropy axis.
v1_finding: Gaussian-edge-weight perturbation of ring C_N produces near-isotropic spectral shift; on/off-axis amplitude ratio 0.96-0.98 across eps in [0.01, 0.5]; no direction shows strict K-signature on this construction.
v2_finding: Off-centre observer on unit ring substrate sees Class K signature (strict three-criteria pass at eps in [0.005, 0.4]; r^2 ~ 1.000; eps_fit matches input eps to 4 decimals). On-axis observer sees pure circular motion (K-signature absent at eps < 0.4). Discriminator works.
verdict: A1 PASSES at the projective-substrate-with-offset-observer construction. A1 FAILS at the perturbed-cascade-Laplacian construction. The geometric mechanism is observer-position-on-substrate-ring, NOT directional-perturbation-of-substrate-density.

anomaly_R1_R2_outside_standard_range: R1 (sin/2 = 0.157) and R2 (tan = 0.331) give eccentricities outside the standard cosmic range; these would constitute substantial departures from observed quasi-isotropy. R3 is the only reading consistent with both physical K-range AND standard cosmic eccentricity range.
description: Closed-form geometric inversion of 18.3 deg separation
preferred_reading_rationale: R3 reading gives eps_AoE = 0.0506 — in the standard cosmic eccentricity range (0.01 < eps < 0.1), and matches the Antikythera lunar eccentricity (0.054) to 1%. The R3 form 1-cos(theta) is the canonical Hopf-bundle aperture for a fiber over a base direction; this maps cleanly onto MFO §VII.4.1.1 substrate-bundle framework.
verdict: A2 PARTIAL PASS at R3 reading; FAIL at R1/R2 readings. The geometric framing matters: R3 (Hopf bundle aperture) gives a clean physical eps_AoE = 0.0506 indistinguishable from canonical Class K eccentricities.

consistency_check_against_R1: eps_R1 = 0.157 vs matter-drift upper = 0.00428: ratio 36.7x — INCONSISTENT at R1 reading.
consistency_check_against_R2: eps_R2 = 0.331 vs matter-drift upper = 0.00428: ratio 77.3x — INCONSISTENT at R2 reading.
consistency_check_against_R3: eps_R3 = 0.0506 vs matter-drift upper = 0.00428: ratio 11.8x — STILL INCONSISTENT at R3 reading.
interpretation_option_a: Partition-for-understanding HAS A COUNTER-EXAMPLE at AoE: matter-drift and medium-push readings give incompatible eps_AoE estimates; they cannot both be true at the same frame of substrate-coupling. One of the two has a hidden assumption failure.
interpretation_option_b: Partition-for-understanding survives IF the two readings are not 'partitions of the same substrate at AoE' but rather 'partitions of different substrate-coupling channels' — matter-drift sees only the matter-particle channel (UHECR), medium-push sees the substrate-rate channel (CMB anisotropy). Then both can be true; they are just measuring different observables, and the 'eps_AoE' from each measures something different at the substrate level.
interpretation_option_c: The 18.3 deg AoE-dipole separation is NOT an eps_AoE geometric signature at all — it's a systematic alignment (Bennett 2011 reading) that has no substrate-level geometric content. Then F3's inconsistency simply reflects that there is no shared substrate-level claim to be consistent about.
load_bearing_consequence: F3's failure forces a conductor decision: which interpretation a/b/c does the framework commit to? Option (b) is the cleanest survival of partition-for-understanding, but it constrains what eps_AoE means at each channel — they can no longer be naively compared.
verdict: F3 FALSIFIED at all three Q2 readings. Matter-drift reading cannot match medium-push reading for ANY of the three geometric inversions of the 18.3 deg separation. The factor-of-11-to-77x discrepancy is too large to attribute to error bars.

This suggests that even R3 is INCOMPATIBLE with strict Saadeh isotropy at the quadrupole level — the AoE-direction substrate eccentricity claim is tension with observed isotropy at large angular scales.
